mechanism_narrative: A continued drop in WORKPLACES mobility signals fewer weekday trips and weaker lunchtime demand, which lowers RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to the prior four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES remains below its current four-week average and does not recover by at least 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility is above its recent level, more people stay home and shift discretionary shopping online or defer visits, reducing retail-and-recreation outings within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds its prior 4-week mean by at least 1 point for two consecutive weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL stays above its trailing four-week average for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates suppressed commuting and fewer downtown trips; together these reduce exposure to retail corridors and push RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay below their current four-week means.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT falls sharply below its recent baseline, it marks a new restriction or service disruption regime that weakens access to shopping districts and depresses RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points week-on-week and stays below -35
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 7 days after TRANSIT crosses below -35 and drops more than 5 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS mobility crowds out indoor leisure only temporarily, but when PARKS and RETAIL_REC both remain depressed, the shared signal indicates broad demand weakness that keeps RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite PARKS staying below its trailing average and no recovery in indoor mobility proxies.

mechanism_narrative: Late-summer cooling or weather deterioration reduces park visits first and then retail leisure outings, so a drop in PARKS over one week predicts lower RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -15 after being above -10 in the previous week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not weaken within 14 days after PARKS drops below -15 from a less negative prior week.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM declines alongside RESIDENTIAL rising, households are consolidating trips and spending more time at home, which leads to fewer discretionary retail visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM stays below its four-week mean and RESIDENTIAL stays above it.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both stabilize after recent declines, the system has passed the immediate shock phase and retail mobility should recover modestly within four weeks as routine commuting resumes.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT each rise for two consecutive weeks after being below -35
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next 28 days despite both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rising for two consecutive weeks from below -35.
